title: After we had eaten, we went for a walk

lines.en: Bruno, do you remember Sunday? After we had finished lunch, we walked into Phoenix Park.
lines.pt: Bruno, você lembra do domingo? Depois de termos terminado o almoço, fomos andando até o Phoenix Park.

lines.en: Of course! Before we had gone very far, we saw the wild deer under the trees.
lines.pt: Claro! Antes de termos ido muito longe, vimos os cervos selvagens debaixo das árvores.

lines.en: Yes! Once the deer had noticed us, they moved slowly away across the grass.
lines.pt: Sim! Assim que os cervos nos notaram, eles se afastaram devagar pela grama.

lines.en: After I had taken a few photos, I realised my phone battery was nearly empty.
lines.pt: Depois de eu ter tirado algumas fotos, percebi que a bateria do celular estava quase vazia.

lines.en: Then we found a bench near the pond, because we had been walking for an hour.
lines.pt: Depois achamos um banco perto do lago, porque tínhamos andado por uma hora.

lines.en: Before I had even sat down, a dog ran past me and stole my biscuit!
lines.pt: Antes de eu ter sequer sentado, um cachorro passou correndo e roubou meu biscoito!

lines.en: I laughed so much! Once the owner had caught the dog, he apologised and offered us ice cream.
lines.pt: Eu ri tanto! Assim que o dono pegou o cachorro, ele se desculpou e nos ofereceu sorvete.

lines.en: That was kind. After we had eaten the ice cream, we watched some children play Gaelic football.
lines.pt: Foi gentil. Depois de termos tomado o sorvete, vimos algumas crianças jogarem futebol gaélico.

lines.en: They were good! By the time they had finished, the sun had gone behind the clouds.
lines.pt: Eles eram bons! Quando terminaram, o sol já tinha ido para trás das nuvens.

lines.en: And before we had reached the gate, it had started to rain heavily.
lines.pt: E antes de termos chegado ao portão, já tinha começado a chover forte.

lines.en: Typical Dublin! Once we had dried off at home, we agreed it was a perfect day.
lines.pt: Típico de Dublin! Assim que nos secamos em casa, concordamos que foi um dia perfeito.

facts.label: Sequência no passado
facts.sub: Depois de termos comido: After we had eaten. Antes de termos chegado: Before we had arrived. Assim que tínhamos…: Once we had…

facts.label: Depois de ter…
facts.sub: After + had + particípio dá a ação anterior: After we had eaten, we went out. Em português, “depois de termos comido”. Depois da vírgula, use o passado simples. After também pode ficar no meio da frase.

facts.label: Antes de ter…
facts.sub: Before + had + particípio dá o que ainda não tinha acontecido: Before we had reached the gate, it started to rain. Muitas vezes o passado simples também é possível, mas had deixa a sequência bem clara.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “After we had eaten” means we ate first.
After is followed by the future in past stories.
items.why: We use had + participle or the past simple.

items.s: “Once the deer had noticed us” means the deer noticed us first.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “After we had eaten” means we ate first. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After is followed by the future in past stories. → Falso (We use had + participle or the past simple.)
“Once the deer had noticed us” means the deer noticed us first. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Telling the story of a day in the park · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Monday evening in a small flat in Dublin. Gil and Lia are drinking tea at the kitchen table. Photos from Sunday are open on Lia’s phone. They went to Phoenix Park, one of the biggest city parks in Europe. So many things happened on that walk. They tell the day again, step by step.

“Lia, do you remember Sunday? After we had finished lunch, we walked into Phoenix Park.” says Gil. “Of course! Before we had gone very far, we saw the wild deer under the trees.” says Lia. “Yes! Once the deer had noticed us, they moved slowly away across the grass.” says Gil.
